audit.whatIsWrong: Four places attribute Mega Gnar's unconditional AoE stun to GNAR! (spikes[1].text, mid, whys[4], and wants.foe[1] via 'the GNAR! AOE stun'): 'GNAR!'s AOE stun cancels your entire kite'.
audit.why: GNAR! only stuns enemies it slams into terrain — Riot's text is 'Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage.' In open ground it is a knockback and a slow. The unconditional area stun is Wallop, Mega Gnar's W, on a 7s cooldown. Getting this backwards costs Mel the single best piece of counterplay in the matchup: choosing where to stand. Fought away from walls his ultimate is survivable; fought in the tri-brush or against the lane wall it is a stun plus bonus damage.
audit.corrected: Wallop is the 7s unconditional AoE stun; GNAR! stuns only against a wall, so hold fights in open ground.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five places say Gnar's hops dodge Solar Snare and treat it as a permanent condition — 'don't waste E hoping to root him on cooldown'. No cooldown is ever given.
audit.why: Hop is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12 while Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9. At rank 1 Mel's root returns twice for every Hop, so the dodge is a once-per-22-seconds answer, not a standing property. The second snare inside that window lands. Same shape as the Gangplank cleanse maths and equally decisive.
audit.corrected: Hop is 22s at rank 1 against an 11s Solar Snare — the second root inside the window lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] says to use W to 'destroy and return his Boomerang' but stops at the damage.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'If he catches the boomerang its cooldown is reduced.' Reflecting or destroying it in flight denies the catch, so Boomerang Throw goes on its full 16s at rank 1 instead of a refunded one. That is the mechanism that actually breaks his mini-form poke pattern, and it is worth far more than the reflected damage.
audit.corrected: Denying the catch keeps Boomerang Throw on its full cooldown instead of a refunded one.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer dosFull[1].t instructs 'Reflect GNAR! (Mega) back the moment he commits'.
audit.why: GNAR! throws the enemies around him in a direction — it displaces units rather than firing a projectile at Mel, so it is not what Rebuttal returns. Boomerang Throw is the projectile in this kit and the one worth spending a 38s cooldown on. Pointing the reflect at the ultimate wastes it on the one cast it cannot answer.
audit.corrected: Point the reflect at Boomerang Throw.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gnar.json (Q 'throws a boomerang'; R 'throws everything around him')

audit.whatIsWrong: Flagged in the packet: the level chart gives Gnar five of seven stages while the matchup sits at 85.71%.
audit.why: Two stages are contradicted by the entry's own reasoning rather than by the win rate alone. Level 3 is the stage Rebuttal comes online, and Boomerang Throw is Gnar's only mini-form poke — a reflect that also denies the catch refund makes that stage a read, not a loss. First item, whys[5] already describes as 'you can only punish when he whiffs a boomerang into your root', which is skill expression, not a clean Gnar stage. I moved only those two to Skill and left levels 1, 2 and 6 with Gnar, because his early range advantage and the Mega transform are real and I will not invent a power shift to chase a 7-game sample.
audit.corrected: win[2] and win[5] Gnar -> Skill; final chart Gnar 3 / Skill 3 / Mel 1.

Boomerang Throw flies further than your Q barrage and his hops sidestep Solar Snare, so don't waste E hoping to root him on cooldown — bank it for when he commits a boomerang animation and can't reposition. Soak Q poke at max range, build Overwhelm slowly, and accept that levels 2-3 are his: he chunks you faster than you stack him. Hold W to delete his next Boomerang and bounce it back rather than burning it on a shield.

notes: Two corrections here change how the matchup is played. First, the entry credited GNAR! with an unconditional AoE stun in four places; GNAR! only stuns enemies slammed into terrain, and the unconditional stun is Wallop (7s). That makes 'fight him away from walls' the real counterplay, which was nowhere in the data. Second, Hop is 22s at rank 1 against Solar Snare's 11s, so 'his hops dodge your snare' is a once-per-window answer rather than a standing property — the second root lands. Also added the Boomerang catch mechanic: reflecting it in flight denies the catch that refunds its cooldown, which is worth more than the reflected damage. On the flagged chart contradiction (Gnar 5/7 stages at an 85.71% win rate over only 7 games) I moved just two stages to Skill, each justified by the entry's own reasoning rather than by the win rate, and deliberately left levels 1, 2 and 6 with Gnar rather than invent a power shift to chase a small sample. Full-layer verdict fields remain uncorrectable through the applier (shared boilerplate, exactly-once rule).
